20:
Zheng He was the most outstanding navigator in Chinese history, displaying extraordinary wisdom and outstanding ability in many fields, including navigation, diplomacy and military affairs. He led a huge fleet on seven long voyages, visiting many countries and regions in the Western Pacific and the Indian Ocean and deepening mutual understanding between China and Southeast Asia and East Africa.

Zheng He's voyages to the Western Seas played a very positive role in promoting economic and cultural exchanges between China and other countries and made a great contribution to maintaining regional peace. To remember Zheng He and his great achievements forever, 11 July—the day Zheng He first set sail with his fleet—has been designated China's Maritime Day.
21: Xu Xiake was a famous geographer of the Ming Dynasty. He spent more than thirty years travelling over more than half of China. Mainly on foot, he visited many remote and out-of-the-way areas. He recorded his observations and the results of his investigations in detail, leaving later generations precious research material. Through field surveys of many rivers he corrected errors about water sources in earlier documents. He also described in detail how such factors as landform and climate affect plants, and vividly depicted scenic spots, historic sites and local customs around the country. His records were compiled by later generations into The Travels of Xu Xiake, which has had a wide influence at home and abroad.
22:
The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau lies in southwest China. It covers an area of about 2.3 million square kilometres and has an average elevation of over 4,000 metres, and is known as the "roof of the world". The plateau is rich in natural resources and has beautiful scenery, and is home to many rare wild animals.

Temperatures on the plateau are very low, which has created large areas of alpine glaciers. It is the source of many famous Asian rivers and the main source of fresh water for China and Southeast Asia. The plateau is vital to the global ecosystem.

Under the impact of climate change, the glaciers on the plateau are melting faster. China has been working hard to protect the plateau's ecosystem: grassland coverage has been increasing, and many endangered species are now more effectively protected.
23:
The Loess Plateau is the third largest plateau in China. It covers about 600,000 square kilometres and has an average elevation of 1,000 to 2,000 metres. Most of it is covered with loess 50 to 80 metres thick, making it the area with the most concentrated loess and the thickest loess cover in the world. It is a miracle created by nature and is unique in the world.

The Loess Plateau is one of the birthplaces of the Chinese nation. As early as 5,500 years ago people had already begun farming there. With the continuous development of farming, the population of the plateau kept growing, and by the Qin and Han dynasties it had become the political and economic centre of China. Today, with the implementation of the strategy for developing the western region, the economy of the Loess Plateau area has developed rapidly.
24:
The Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau lies mostly within Yunnan and Guizhou provinces. With a total area of about 500,000 square kilometres and an average elevation of 2,000 to 4,000 metres, it is the fourth largest plateau in China. The plateau is high in the west and low in the east, and its many rivers have cut many deep, steep canyons. Much of the soil in the canyons is fertile and very suitable for growing a wide range of crops.

The plateau's unique natural environment has created both biological and cultural diversity. It is an area of China rich in forest and mineral resources and an important region for the origin of early humans. The plateau is home to more ethnic minorities than any other part of China, and each group has preserved its own rich and varied cultural traditions.
25: Putting up Spring Festival couplets is an important custom observed by the Chinese at Spring Festival. A couplet consists of a pair of poetic lines and a four-character horizontal scroll. The lines and the scroll are written in gold or black on red paper: red stands for good luck and gold for wealth. The couplets are pasted on both sides of the front door and above the door frame. The lines reflect the features of traditional Chinese poetry, with the two lines having the same number of characters and related content. The horizontal scroll highlights the theme of the couplet and adds the finishing touch. In concise language the couplets paint vivid images and express fine wishes. When every household puts up couplets, people know that Spring Festival has officially begun.
26: Since ancient times the seal has been a proof of identity and a symbol of power in China. A seal is not only practical but also a form of art—an ancient art combining calligraphy and engraving—and is often regarded as an independent work of art on a par with painting and calligraphy. From the choice of material to the craft of making and the design of the characters, seals offer extremely rich aesthetic expression. Artists in other countries usually sign their paintings, whereas Chinese artists often stamp a seal on their paintings and calligraphy instead of signing. In this way the seal becomes part of the work and a means of expressing its uniqueness.
27: The headquarters building of China Central Television is located in Chaoyang District, Beijing, with a total floor area of about 550,000 square metres. The main building consists of two towers, and thanks to its distinctive shape it has become a popular attraction in the city, drawing many visitors every day. The innovative structure of the building is the fruit of long-term cooperation between Chinese and foreign architects; it not only reflects environmental awareness but also greatly saves building materials. CCTV has a dedicated route running through the building that shows the public the various studios and the history of the broadcaster. There visitors can also enjoy spectacular views of the Forbidden City and other parts of Beijing.
28:
The Lugou Bridge, 15 kilometres southwest of Tiananmen Square, spans the Yongding River and is the oldest surviving multi-arch stone bridge in Beijing.

The bridge was first completed in 1192 and rebuilt in 1698. It is supported by 281 pillars, each with a stone lion on top. On the heads, backs, bellies and paws of these lions hide even more lions. Lifelike and varied in posture, these lions are the finest examples of the bridge's stone carving. There are countless stone lions on the bridge, hence the saying popular in Beijing: "the stone lions on the Lugou Bridge—too many to count".

The Lugou Bridge is famous not only for its aesthetic features but is also recognized as a monument in the history of stone bridge construction.
29:
The Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge is the first road-rail bridge over the Yangtze designed by China and built with domestically produced materials. Its upper four-lane road deck is 4,589 metres long and its lower double-track railway deck is 6,772 metres long. The railway bridge links the former Tianjin-Pukou and Shanghai-Nanjing lines, shortening the river crossing by train from an hour and a half to two minutes. The bridge is an important hub for north-south traffic and one of Nanjing's famous attractions.

The completion of the bridge marked a leap forward in China's bridge building. It has greatly facilitated the exchange of goods and the movement of people across the Yangtze and has played a huge role in promoting economic development and improving people's lives.
30:
The Zhaozhou Bridge was built in the Sui Dynasty, around 605 AD. It is 50.82 metres long and 9.6 metres wide, with a span of 37.37 metres. The gifted architect Li Chun designed the bridge and supervised its construction. The bridge is novel in structure and graceful in form. It has one large arch, with two smaller arches at each end of it that help discharge floodwater, reduce the weight of the bridge and save stone. Since its completion the bridge has withstood many floods and earthquakes, yet its main structure remains intact and it is still in use today.

The Zhaozhou Bridge was a pioneering work in the history of bridge building in the world and an outstanding achievement of ancient Chinese civilization. Bridges of similar design did not appear in Europe until the 14th century, more than 700 years later.
31: The site of the First National Congress of the Communist Party of China is at No. 76 Xingye Road, Shanghai. It is a typical Shanghai-style residence built in the autumn of 1920. On 23 July 1921 the First National Congress of the Communist Party of China was held here. The congress adopted the Party's first programme and first resolution, elected the central leading body and proclaimed the birth of the Communist Party of China. In September 1952 the site was restored, and a memorial hall was set up and opened to the public. Besides introducing the delegates to the congress, the hall also presents the course of the Party's historical development, and has become a patriotic education base for learning about Party history and remembering the revolutionary martyrs.
32: Yan'an lies in northern Shaanxi Province, on the middle reaches of the Yellow River, and is a sacred place of the Chinese revolution. Mao Zedong and other revolutionaries of the older generation lived and fought here for thirteen years, leading the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the War of Liberation, fostering the Yan'an Spirit and making a great contribution to the Chinese revolution. Yan'an has the largest number, the widest distribution and the highest rank of revolutionary sites in the country. It is a national education base for patriotism, revolutionary tradition and the Yan'an Spirit. Yan'an has nine revolutionary memorial halls, which house large numbers of important objects left by the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the older generation of revolutionaries during the Yan'an period, and therefore enjoys the reputation of being a "city of museums of the Chinese revolution".
33: Jinggangshan lies at the border of Hunan and Jiangxi provinces and is known as the "red cradle of the Chinese revolution" for its glorious revolutionary history. In October 1927, Mao Zedong, Zhu De and other revolutionaries of the older generation led the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army here and waged an arduous struggle. They created the first rural revolutionary base area, lit the sparks of the Chinese revolution and opened up the revolutionary road with Chinese characteristics—"encircling the cities from the countryside and seizing power by armed force"—and from here the Chinese revolution advanced towards victory. Jinggangshan now has more than 100 revolutionary sites and has become a "revolutionary history museum without walls", an important base for education in patriotism and revolutionary tradition.
34:
Hainan is China's second largest island after Taiwan and the southernmost province of the country. The island has beautiful scenery, a pleasant climate, abundant sunshine, rich biodiversity, numerous hot springs and clear seawater. Most of its beaches are ideal for swimming and sunbathing almost all year round, so the island is known as China's four-season garden and holiday resort and attracts large numbers of Chinese and foreign tourists every year.

Since Hainan became a province in 1988, its tourism, service and high-tech industries have developed rapidly, and it is China's only provincial-level special economic zone. With the strong support of the central government and the people of the whole country, Hainan will be built into China's largest pilot free trade zone.
35:
Qinghai is a province in northwest China with an average elevation of over 3,000 metres, most of which is high mountains and plateaus. The province is named after Qinghai Lake, the largest saltwater lake in the country. Known as "the most beautiful lake in China", Qinghai Lake is one of the most popular tourist attractions and a paradise for photographers and artists.

Qinghai has magnificent mountains and rivers, a vast territory and abundant resources, and rich oil and natural gas reserves. The economies of many cities in the province have grown substantially, driven by the oil and gas industry. Qinghai is especially known for its abundant water resources: it is the source of China's three major rivers—the Yangtze, the Yellow River and the Lancang—and plays an important role in China's water ecology.
36:
Yunnan is a province in southwest China with an average elevation of 1,500 metres. It has a long history, beautiful scenery and a pleasant climate. Yunnan has an excellent ecological environment and great biodiversity, and is known as a paradise for wildlife. It also has a variety of mineral deposits and abundant water resources, which provide favourable conditions for the sustainable development of the provincial economy.

Twenty-five ethnic minorities live in Yunnan, most of them with their own languages, customs and religions. Yunnan's unique natural scenery and rich ethnic culture make it one of the most popular tourist destinations in China, attracting large numbers of domestic and foreign tourists every year.
37: The Qinghai-Tibet Railway is the highest and longest plateau railway in the world. With a total length of 1,956 kilometres, 960 of which lie above 4,000 metres, it is the first railway linking Tibet with the rest of China. Because the railway crosses the world's most fragile ecosystem, ecological protection measures were taken both during and after construction to ensure that it is a "green railway". The railway has greatly shortened travel time between the interior of China and Tibet. More importantly, it has greatly boosted Tibet's economic development and improved the lives of local residents. Since the railway opened, more and more people have chosen to travel to Tibet by train, which also gives them a chance to enjoy the scenery along the way.
38: The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge is 55 kilometres long and is an extraordinary engineering feat for China. Linking the three cities, it is the world's longest sea-crossing bridge-and-tunnel system. The bridge cuts travel time between the three cities from three hours to 30 minutes. This huge reinforced concrete bridge fully proves that China is capable of building record-breaking mega-structures. It will boost regional integration and promote economic growth. The bridge is key to China's master plan for developing its own Greater Bay Area, which China hopes to build into a region comparable to the bay areas of San Francisco, New York and Tokyo in technological innovation and economic prosperity.
